title: Coherent smooth pullback comparisons for descended monoscheme towers
statement: Use the monoschemes, toric realizations, centered towers and contraction of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Fix a rule $\mathcal F$ assigning a finite normalized blowup tower to every $\mathbf Q[M]$ for fine torsion-free monoschemes $M$ with finite affine cover, including their finite disjoint unions. Assume that each center is coherent and torus invariant, and that for every smooth scheme morphism between these toric schemes the rule has canonical contracted-pullback comparisons preserving ordered ideals, compatible with identities and composition. Suppose each $\mathcal F(\mathbf Q[M])$ has a unique centered saturated monoscheme lift $\mathcal T(M)$ through the canonical monoid-ideal and blowup-chart identifications, with fine torsion-free intermediate monoschemes having finite affine covers. Then for every smooth monoscheme map $a:N\to M$ there is a canonical comparison $\mathcal T(N)\simeq(a^*\mathcal T(M))^c$ whose toric realization is the specified comparison for $\mathbf Q[a]$. At each retained stage its ideal is the recursively pulled-back monoid ideal and the order is unchanged. The contracted stages correspond exactly on the toric and monoscheme sides: both the unit-center condition and the isomorphism condition are respected, so a nonidentity normalization or saturation is retained. These comparisons respect identities and composition; for $N'\xrightarrow b N\xrightarrow a M$, the successive comparisons agree with that for $ab$, including the identification of successive contractions with the single contracted pullback.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.19, second half, and Theorem 3.2.20, p.106; smoothness in Lemma 3.2.12(i), and contracted pullback in 3.1.21--3.1.23, pp.101--102. No Stacks tag states this monoscheme result.

proof.text: Fix a smooth $a:N\to M$. By [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison](iii), $\mathbf Q[a]$ is smooth, so the assumed scheme comparison is available. Form the full recursive pullback $D=a^*\mathcal T(M)$, keeping all original indices. Clause (i) identifies each extended ring center with the realization of its recursively extended monoid center; clause (ii) identifies the next normalized blowup with the next saturated blowup. This gives an induction, starting with $D_0=N$, identifying $\mathbf Q[D]$ with the full scheme pullback tower. At each step the objects remain fine, torsion free and finitely covered by clause (ii). The stage maps to the original levels remain smooth: in the smooth product charts underlying clause (ii), a chart $P[I-c]^{\rm sat}$ pulls back to $P[I-c]^{\rm sat}\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$. Indeed extension of $I$ adjoins the same differences $d-c$, and taking a positive multiple tests saturation separately in the two factors. Thus the next map again has the smooth stalk form of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. The pulled ideals are coherent and nonempty: extend their finite nonempty generating sets. This justifies repeating clause (ii), rather than assuming a pullback comparison for a nonsmooth intermediate map.

At every index of $D$, clause (i) of [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison] says that the ring center is unit if and only if the monoid center is whole. For a whole center, the chart definition [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] makes the monoscheme arrow the saturation: choose the generator $0$ and obtain $P^{\rm sat}\to P$. Its realized arrow is normalization. By [lem-trf-affine-monoid-algebra-normalization] its ring map is the inclusion $\mathbf Q[P]\subset\mathbf Q[P^{\rm sat}]$. This is an isomorphism exactly when $P=P^{\rm sat}$: surjectivity forces every basis monomial $e^g$, $g\in P^{\rm sat}$, to have exponent in $P$, and the converse is identity. The monoid saturation map is an isomorphism under the same condition, locally on each chart. Hence the two full towers delete precisely the same indices. Contracting them therefore gives canonically corresponding centered towers. This argument does not delete a nonidentity saturation/normalization with whole center, nor a proper principal center whose blowup is already an isomorphism.

Let $r_0<\cdots<r_{s-1}$ be the retained original indices of $D$. The specified scheme comparison identifies $\mathcal F(\mathbf Q[N])$ with this contracted realized tower, so it has $s$ stages. Construct the desired comparison by induction on $j=0,\ldots,s$, maintaining an isomorphism between the $j$th level of $\mathcal T(N)$ and the corresponding level of $D^c$, realizing the specified scheme comparison there. At $j=0$ use $1_N$. At the next center the scheme comparison identifies the actual ideal of $\mathcal F(\mathbf Q[N])$ with the extended ideal at $r_j$. Both are realizations of coherent monoid ideals on the already identified monoscheme. Injectivity in [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison](i) makes these monoid ideals equal, not just their supports. Both next levels are saturated blowups along this same ideal. Apply [lem-trf-saturated-monoscheme-blowup-universal] in both directions: each source is saturated and its center becomes locally principal. Uniqueness makes the two composites identities. This defines the next centered level isomorphism over the previous one.

source.place: 3.2.19, second half, and 3.2.20, p.106; unique principalizing lift in 3.1.21, p.101.

proof.text: The isomorphism just constructed realizes the specified scheme comparison, completing the inductive invariant. To verify this rather than assume fullness of toric realization, use [lem-trf-toric-realization-finite-type]: all the identified levels are reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes with integral components. The centers are nonzero on every component by [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison](i), hence their zero schemes are nowhere dense (the generic stalk of a nonzero ideal in a domain is the whole fraction field). The actual scheme comparison and the realized monoscheme comparison are two isomorphisms over the already identified previous level between the same normalized blowups, by clause (ii). Their quotient is a base automorphism of that normalized blowup, which is identity by [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus]. Thus they agree. Iterating steps 3 and 4 finishes the comparison. The index $j$ corresponds exactly to $r_j$, and its center is the recursive pullback ideal proved equal in step 3. No original index has been permuted.

source.place: 3.2.19--3.2.20, p.106; normalized blowup universal property 2.2.2--2.2.8, pp.89--91.

proof.text: The comparison is unique with its base identity, retained index map and actual centers. At each retained stage two candidates differ by an automorphism over the preceding level of a saturated blowup. By [lem-trf-saturated-monoscheme-blowup-universal] this automorphism is identity. Induction from the base gives equality of all level maps. For $a=1_M$, step 1 pulls back every center to itself and every chart map is identity. The toric identity comparison equates the lengths of $\mathcal F(\mathbf Q[M])$ and its contraction; by step 2 no stage of its monoscheme lift is deleted either. Thus the constructed comparison for $1_M$ is the identity by this uniqueness. This also proves that every assigned lift is already contracted.

source.place: 3.1.21--3.1.22, p.101; identity case of functoriality in 3.2.19--3.2.20, p.106.

proof.text: For $N'\xrightarrow b N\xrightarrow a M$, compare the full successive pullback with the full pullback along $ab$. Extended ideals agree: both are generated by images of the original sections, so $b^*(a^*I)=(ab)^*I$. At the first next level, both constructions are saturated blowups of that same ideal; [lem-trf-saturated-monoscheme-blowup-universal] gives their unique isomorphism over $N'$. Inductively apply this to every next center and level. A stage deleted after the first pullback has whole ideal and an isomorphism arrow; its smooth pullback again has whole ideal and is an isomorphism, by the smooth-pullback compatibility in [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison](ii). Removing it before the second pullback therefore changes neither a later ideal nor a later level: the connecting isomorphism identifies that later ideal with its extension across the deleted level. Conversely every index not yet deleted is removed by the second contraction exactly when both deletion conditions hold after $ab$. Thus the successive contractions and the single contraction retain the same subsequence of original indices, with canonical identifications of all intervening levels. This includes consecutive deleted indices and length-zero towers.

Under the identification of step 6, the composite of the two comparisons and the comparison for $ab$ are centered ordered isomorphisms from $\mathcal T(N')$ to $((ab)^*\mathcal T(M))^c$, over $1_{N'}$. They have the same retained indices: the toric composition law gives the same retained scheme indices, and step 2 identifies them with the monoscheme indices. They preserve the same ideals by step 3 and the equality of extensions in step 6. The uniqueness argument of step 5, applying [lem-trf-saturated-monoscheme-blowup-universal] at each retained level, therefore makes all their maps equal. Their realizations are the prescribed scheme composite by step 4 and the assumed toric composition law. This proves the claimed composition coherence, including the identification of contractions. All arguments are componentwise and admit empty covers; on an empty input a unit saturation is identity and the identity comparison forces the assigned tower to have length zero.

source.place: 3.1.22--3.1.23, p.101; 3.2.19--3.2.20, p.106: composition and empty-input cases made explicit.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.19--3.1.23, printed p.101; 3.2.19--3.2.20, printed p.106. Expanded induction and coherence details.
